verses.text: The whole Israelite crew gathered at Shiloh and set up the Meeting Tent there. The land was under their control. 🏕️
But seven tribes still hadn’t received their land shares. 👥
Joshua told Israel, ‘How long are you going to put off taking possession of the land Yahweh, your ancestors’ God, has given you? 🕰️
‘Pick three men from each tribe. I’ll send them to walk through the land and map out each tribe’s share. Then they’ll come back to me. 🗺️
‘They’ll divide the land into seven sections. Judah will stay in its territory in the south, and Joseph’s family in its territory in the north. 🗺️
‘Survey the land in seven parts and bring the report back here. I’ll cast lots for you here before Yahweh our God. 🎲

‘The Levites don’t get a land share among you; their inheritance is serving as Yahweh’s priests. Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh already received the land east of the Jordan that Moses, Yahweh’s servant, gave them.’ 🛐
The surveyors headed out. Joshua told them, ‘Go walk the land, survey it, and come back to me. I’ll cast lots for you here at Shiloh, before Yahweh.’ 🗣️
They went through the land, mapped it town by town, and recorded it in a book as seven sections. Then they came back to Joshua at the Shiloh camp. 📜
Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before Yahweh. There he divided the land among Israel’s tribes, share by share. 🎲
Benjamin’s tribe got the first lot, by its families. Its land sat between Judah’s people and Joseph’s people. 🗺️
Its north border started at the Jordan, went up along the north side of Jericho, climbed west through the hill country, and ended at the Beth-aven wilderness. 🏔️
From there the border passed Luz—also called Bethel—on its south side, then went down to Ataroth-addar by the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon. 🗺️
It stretched west and curved south from the mountain facing Beth-horon, ending at Kiriath-baal—also called Kiriath-jearim—a town belonging to Judah. That was the west side. 🏙️
The south side started at the far end of Kiriath-jearim. The border ran west to the spring at Nephtoah, 💧
then down to the mountain edge facing Hinnom Valley, north of Rephaim Valley. It went down Hinnom Valley along Jerusalem’s south side, then down to En-rogel. 🗺️
The border stretched north to En-shemesh and Geliloth, opposite the Adummim Pass, then went down to the Stone of Bohan, Reuben’s son. 🪨
It passed along the north side facing the Arabah, then went down into the Arabah. 🗺️
The line passed north of Beth-hoglah and ended at the Salt Sea’s north bay, where the Jordan ends. That was Benjamin’s southern border. 🌊
The Jordan River was Benjamin’s east border. That was Benjamin’s inheritance, with its borders all around, by family. 🌊
Benjamin’s towns by family were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, and Emek-keziz; 🏘️
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, and Bethel; 🏘️
Avvim, Parah, and Ophrah; 🏘️
Chephar-ammoni, Ophni, and Geba—twelve towns altogether, plus their villages. 🏘️
Gibeon, Ramah, and Beeroth; 🏘️
Mizpeh, Chephirah, and Mozah; 🏘️
Rekem, Irpeel, and Taralah; 🏘️
Zelah, Eleph, Jebus—the same as Jerusalem—Gibeath, and Kiriath. That’s fourteen towns, plus their villages. This was Benjamin’s inheritance by family. 🏘️
